email.subject: We posted a new notice for your account
email.body:
Account update
We posted a new notice for your account
Here's what it's about

An Insufficient Funds Notice posted for your account ending in (...2311)
We encourage you to read the entire notice because it contains specific information about your account.
View your notice in two ways
• From Chase Mobile go to your profile and choose "Statements and documents."
• At chase.com/statements, just sign in to your account.
You'll see your notice under "Notices and letters".
If you aren't enrolled to receive Paperless Statements and Notices, or think you're getting this message in error, please visit chase.com/CustomerService for ways to contact us.
Securely access your accounts with the Chase Mobile® app or chase.com.
About this message

Chase Mobile® app is available for select mobile devices. Message and data rates may apply.

This service email gives you updates and information about your Chase relationship.

Chase cannot guarantee the delivery of alerts and notifications. Wireless or internet service provider outages or other circumstances could delay them. You can always check chase.com or the Chase Mobile app for the status of your accounts including your latest account balances and transaction details.

To protect your personal information, please don't reply to this message. Chase won't ask for confidential information in an email.

If you have concerns about the authenticity of this message or have questions about your account visit chase.com/CustomerService for ways to contact us.

Your privacy is important to us. See our online Security Center to learn how to protect your information.

JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. Member FDIC

© 2026 JPMorgan Chase & Co.

email.subject: Meet our new Scientific Advisory Board
email.body:
Hey there,​Here’s a money-printing secret THEY don’t want you to know:​You can persuade people of almost anything if you convince them science is on your side.​Supplement marketing proves it.​It’s thick with phrases like “science-based,” “evidence-based,” and “clinically dosed” because those words sell.​Most shoppers can’t or won’t check the research, so the slogans do their job.​And that’s the problem.​Most supplement companies don’t actually want to be backed by science—they just want to prance and preen in a science skinsuit.​Legion has always tried to do the harder thing:​Use truly effective ingredients and doses, disclose everything, test every product, and explain the evidence plainly.​Now we’re adding another layer of scrutiny.​We created a [Scientific Advisory Board](https://legionathletics.com/scientific-advisory-board/) with five experts in exercise science, sports nutrition, human nutrition, dietetics, and medicine.​Their job isn’t to rubber-stamp whatever lands in their inbox.​It’s to analyze and optimize formulas, challenge claims, and flag anything they wouldn’t feel comfortable defending.​In other words, they’re here to ask hard questions before you have to.​Want to see who’s on our board and how it works?​Go here:​⇒ https://legionathletics.com/scientific-advisory-board/​Enjoy!​Mike MatthewsFounder of Legion​P.S. Some supplements are science-based. Many are just science fiction. Meet the five experts keeping Legion on the nonfiction shelf [here](https://legionathletics.com/scientific-advisory-board/).

email.subject:
Your July Pulumi Roundup: Spend Limits for Neo, Passkeys, Token
 Expiry Policies + Safer ESC Changes
email.body:
New Controls for Agents and Secrets

July 2026

Hi friend,

The last few months put AI agents at the center of Pulumi. July was about keeping them, and the secrets and credentials underneath, under control. You can now cap how much Neo spends in a month, sign in to Pulumi Cloud with a passkey, enforce a maximum lifetime on every access token, and preview an ESC change on a real stack before it ships.

Key Product Updates

-

Preview ESC Changes Before They Ship (https://info.pulumi.com/e3t/Ctc/GC+113/cx72f04/VVpxST5s9mk6W6nDTNt7gMy3dW2v98dD5S641YN1zSXsY3prCCW7Y8-PT6lZ3lHW6nsvQ85jG6yMW5m90FV8HLkdYW5GdbJg46CCJTW3R6ZX94v08qGVdvZzS5XR325W1TyVqn278WkrN2dSRSh2g6D4W84S4Td6T3KHQN1rhP7Yk091BW251n3b10h4CsW7_rZbG6NL1HfW7lxQrj3GXSG6W6JYH0t2K5x1RW6qbtdj4ymly_W5g_Rc17hFWNkW6cWlrT2nWNjcW2nDZ1X6wSCkrW4PMsfL1BVbVWN7YgsP8g7VmPW2Fnxf92y2BdBW2sQ9ng21Z39jW1hZprW8Q7srMW4bC_QP1NTGWYW7Vd7gP7bTj-JVKCC9X4jHPV4W491pCG68R6zwf5pLDWH04 )  A new --override-env flag lets you swap in a draft environment and run pulumi preview or pulumi up against it, so a reviewer can test a configuration change on a real stack before it is approved. Reference a draft with @draft:<draft-id>, and layer several overrides at once.

-

Sign in to Pulumi Cloud with Passkeys (https://info.pulumi.com/e3t/Ctc/GC+113/cx72f04/VVpxST5s9mk6W6nDTNt7gMy3dW2v98dD5S641YN1zSXsF3prCCW7lCdLW6lZ3nBVqWmLj1rJDB0W5YrRs58Z5JhtW1BbNrm8h7l0lN2Fg7W73wzXtN70kHKznfDrnW29ZF3r2grSR3W6ZMMTG6WtTGxW3VP2xb5jtrgWW8W9ftb2kfnpvW97hv5F8KYn3qW3YZnK143Q8wjVcw-3H3ZY7L-W1zdLkL59BsshW6j-xfS8CvgTxW85NnbR8SpCMhW43d8wp6BPwvQW1lks2b4t7hMRW70kHbb69cn5dW88pZcx38DsthVPcm5S5f9rWqW5h0W3p6CbD2fN1nxJQh2Lq_0VF62K_4HldH2MLXd0TVTm69f4W8dVK04 )  Email and password users can now add a passkey and sign in with a biometric or hardware key. Passkeys bind to Pulumi's domain, so they are phishing-resistant by design and remove the shared-secret risk that comes with passwords.

-

Enforce Access Token Expiry Policies (https://info.pulumi.com/e3t/Ctc/GC+113/cx72f04/VVpxST5s9mk6W6nDTNt7gMy3dW2v98dD5S641YN1zSXsF3prCCW7lCdLW6lZ3m4W2b9_sK8nyD5DW3npRDc3Wp7HrW1Mny343JpRywW1vSLj83kj7m_W4c7PDN3NgV2CW3PkYy14FTBf9W67nc6y1Y4TBRN3H6_6WLh5nxW7mt_tx5WR9hsW35B6Bz9c89y5W2bSgMr54gl64W9hjwPw75YTwCW2j6cS48cBw4xN7ClHJd-qdxZW3WH3sB7-5qdQW3r8vgG4gmPSPW6Vg1Fg6MnV6-W8PkzZk45H_SzN9klrjt_LR70W3TBRdK7hSszKW7r5NdK2qlTKbW1PQsmL9fm8_1W8YHg9f7xFwkMW14SJ9L3vsS31f9gycBY04 )  Organization admins can now set a maximum lifetime for every token: personal, organization, and team. Compliance is checked on each request, and any token past the limit is rejected with a clear error, so credential rotation is enforced at the platform level.

Spotlight: Usage Limits for Pulumi Neo

Neo can plan and deploy real infrastructure on its own, and now you can put a budget around it. Set a monthly dollar limit for your organization and Neo pauses when it is reached. Add per-member limits so no single person can spend the whole pool, and get email alerts at 50, 80, 95, and 100 percent of the organization threshold. Admins and billing owners get a clear ceiling on AI agent spend without turning the agent off.

Read the announcement → (https://info.pulumi.com/e3t/Ctc/GC+113/cx72f04/VVpxST5s9mk6W6nDTNt7gMy3dW2v98dD5S641YN1zSXsl3prCCW6N1vHY6lZ3ndW4pp-sW1XhdsRW1jbSJk5fx2x4W92Wbfr5RK6CCW4fD3kl4P9Ln4W3XMryy5LQpwSW6bS13T2kKMW9W2XwbjL1lpc5dW4V8bb13d6QMXW9fNXkc6Dz2R7W8W_7Rb7sZsW2N6FywNDr-Kj0W5XbZQ_5nv-72W68xw-810nGW_VTLwtV7JvPMTN24vqQ0zv-LrW6vmLlv47TSpqN55CVBgkJd0XW8ZwDn23cTKx8VpnTyB7yzp8FW2Mj49s72BZMWVBTxtq11PnHKW6yq4_924_wTzf7gQ31q04 )

Good to Know

-

The Standalone ESC CLI Is Retiring (https://info.pulumi.com/e3t/Ctc/GC+113/cx72f04/VVpxST5s9mk6W6nDTNt7gMy3dW2v98dD5S641YN1zSXsF3prCCW7lCdLW6lZ3lSW764fDJ8HhWBRW26Shpd6l-KJdW6T63fK2snhm2W72Y2-T3mqy0cW7J_djW6JWTHFW2-y_X81FNMs9W6d1GVw83Yl4VW1_HJk_7CX3yQW7JFJfh3rl9HtW2xPJ1_3rmywNN3NZ1FnnSJ8pVgGw8Y5f6j36W7m3cK360ZRGQW2k2B4_7WdbqXW5gbpcf6pNfdXW578gLT2D0165W87w0721sQtdjW2wFksW66fMtJW5g_PR06FZJRfVZKMjV5Y1t18W8rHYV73WZKlYW2-3KbV7kN-xNV64nXV95HrSWW5QVDRH2H_dkvf6czR5204 )  The separate esc CLI has shipped its final release (v0.26.0) and now lives inside the main Pulumi CLI. Replace esc env with pulumi env in your scripts, for example esc env ls becomes pulumi env ls. If you already use the Pulumi CLI, there is nothing to do.

-

Versioned CLI and SDK Docs (https://info.pulumi.com/e3t/Ctc/GC+113/cx72f04/VVpxST5s9mk6W6nDTNt7gMy3dW2v98dD5S641YN1zSXsF3prCCW7lCdLW6lZ3p5W7z9Q7y1811nTW3BW75V8vmV59W6-Ml_03pZ0PsW8bdd7M3PnlwHMnh2_KmjCrSW2hnt113vPDWXW2_9qS-6lBmdQW3LZV8d389L7DW5B24DX7SL1ZBW1Yykd83RCYMdW875_vy2F4jnFW2ThmyK1fpZ9LN6BbrkdFWj06W1xwqQ71m4QKLW5CRzSS38KlPdW4TcsJj9lXy_ZN5vfC4ZkV_kpVxSSB_3Xh02WW61jhRF5tC6MWW224FMG2-m2RFVBQsct26mJt7W2SckT52ZgpR0W62hYYr4QVzVSW2Bv7KZ8X-T5qf5lz-CC04 )  The docs now have a version picker, so you can read the CLI and SDK reference that matches the release you are running instead of only the latest.

Workshops & Webinars

Aug 5Best Practices for Managing Secrets: An Introduction to ESC (https://info.pulumi.com/e3t/Ctc/GC+113/cx72f04/VVpxST5s9mk6W6nDTNt7gMy3dW2v98dD5S641YN1zSXsY3prCCW7Y8-PT6lZ3nmW156Fq22ZCzytN8vnDCf8qLBdW3y7RY62GjCkgN4MP7Rq9NpvlW13bwgq1hY7N3W8c-bv18VdGPsW677ZDw2bwsVKW3XH2h12RT_FRW46Yvsk7M9MVJW6cpjJv50DrQNN3k5VKqfRbtQW7TkRx24T77wsW79FmnJ4BXVDpW42DbYy7p_ywcW8rPhsh8JXbJMW3M8hqw5SkRLbW4DsJ4s7hZqg8W73kHJz1g_lwBW5TYRQj6c-ZGzV1JN2J2ctln0W6h7vRl7Sdv4CW29Hf4F4nF2yhW3px-w51RdXr3MNYrRGXHQxnW4Z5D-62nfw2kW6Bj3D58x6kw2f6FJnRj04 ) : Aggregate, manage, and securely access secrets and configuration from one place.

Aug 12Getting Started with DevOps AI Skills (https://info.pulumi.com/e3t/Ctc/GC+113/cx72f04/VVpxST5s9mk6W6nDTNt7gMy3dW2v98dD5S641YN1zSXsY3prCCW7Y8-PT6lZ3mtW4FxgYV6K6l76W7z-CzG2cBcVlW6jJWjN956SSWW5vGrTk7CvVfCW1fxQYD3HQvcBW44-sH798mN6dW564Z-18SFqQXW61jtR53CfV2QW5-Xlcg1VW8S7W1N1drJ6X2D68W5NhXkl8-5ZryW3WkTNR4VRnzNN45WHH9JnN7GW3wSMGK6vHqJ2W6Zdptz7CcKhYW2tw3Rh5PJtsJW4nyKFy7_SwJFMX2JnRKc528VkPQmn8FX_2qN5-LbNzCbsr-W19p4wn3bLX0nW1-78XY1ml38ZW2jnzNT2msDR1W4bRlbJ7TBpRDW1FJmXv1Df6knW17n8mN96hfw5f1KJWVz04 ) : Set up coding agents with the right hooks, LSP, and Pulumi skills so they produce clean Pulumi code.

Sep 16Neo in a Docker Sandbox: Using Pulumi's Coding Agent for All Things Infra Safely and Securely (https://info.pulumi.com/e3t/Ctc/GC+113/cx72f04/VVpxST5s9mk6W6nDTNt7gMy3dW2v98dD5S641YN1zSXsF3prCCW7lCdLW6lZ3ppW20Sm1x22DqN8W1PpQwm3cBktPW8rmJG483L74PW4qKgbv2wvzdhVlgj_06KwbXFW7blBf26ZkM9TW5D6RVk1gfnFXMf62jX_4vPDW4zky_T8KjRBNW1Pjy7_8z1DqhVzpCHp589HZYW1tyhhB2sNwnbW6qjd613ybK0hW1-0V864yyvsVW77bVx56HmlcBW4G6y6c5Lkx86W3XSXdk86FpPGW897skc4pXvcZW6D9D6J5yBG9sW4J-NHd25Xk0JW7rsrtT4DpjyTW88mstd4KkJT8W6QLY4n35vKvMW4b8_VG2ZNY2Tf6jJB--04 ) : Turn plain-English requests into real cloud infrastructure inside a Docker sandbox, with guardrails.

Community Highlight

New Controls for Agents and Secrets

July 2026

Hi friend,

The last few months put AI agents at the center of Pulumi. July was about keeping them, and the secrets and credentials underneath, under control. You can now cap how much Neo spends in a month, sign in to Pulumi Cloud with a passkey, enforce a maximum lifetime on every access token, and preview an ESC change on a real stack before it ships.

Key Product Updates

-

Preview ESC Changes Before They Ship (https://info.pulumi.com/e3t/Ctc/GC+113/cx72f04/VVpxST5s9mk6W6nDTNt7gMy3dW2v98dD5S641YN1zSXsY3prCCW7Y8-PT6lZ3lHW6nsvQ85jG6yMW5m90FV8HLkdYW5GdbJg46CCJTW3R6ZX94v08qGVdvZzS5XR325W1TyVqn278WkrN2dSRSh2g6D4W84S4Td6T3KHQN1rhP7Yk091BW251n3b10h4CsW7_rZbG6NL1HfW7lxQrj3GXSG6W6JYH0t2K5x1RW6qbtdj4ymly_W5g_Rc17hFWNkW6cWlrT2nWNjcW2nDZ1X6wSCkrW4PMsfL1BVbVWN7YgsP8g7VmPW2Fnxf92y2BdBW2sQ9ng21Z39jW1hZprW8Q7srMW4bC_QP1NTGWYW7Vd7gP7bTj-JVKCC9X4jHPV4W491pCG68R6zwf5pLDWH04 )  A new --override-env flag lets you swap in a draft environment and run pulumi preview or pulumi up against it, so a reviewer can test a configuration change on a real stack before it is approved. Reference a draft with @draft:<draft-id>, and layer several overrides at once.

-

Sign in to Pulumi Cloud with Passkeys (https://info.pulumi.com/e3t/Ctc/GC+113/cx72f04/VVpxST5s9mk6W6nDTNt7gMy3dW2v98dD5S641YN1zSXsF3prCCW7lCdLW6lZ3nBVqWmLj1rJDB0W5YrRs58Z5JhtW1BbNrm8h7l0lN2Fg7W73wzXtN70kHKznfDrnW29ZF3r2grSR3W6ZMMTG6WtTGxW3VP2xb5jtrgWW8W9ftb2kfnpvW97hv5F8KYn3qW3YZnK143Q8wjVcw-3H3ZY7L-W1zdLkL59BsshW6j-xfS8CvgTxW85NnbR8SpCMhW43d8wp6BPwvQW1lks2b4t7hMRW70kHbb69cn5dW88pZcx38DsthVPcm5S5f9rWqW5h0W3p6CbD2fN1nxJQh2Lq_0VF62K_4HldH2MLXd0TVTm69f4W8dVK04 )  Email and password users can now add a passkey and sign in with a biometric or hardware key. Passkeys bind to Pulumi's domain, so they are phishing-resistant by design and remove the shared-secret risk that comes with passwords.

-

Enforce Access Token Expiry Policies (https://info.pulumi.com/e3t/Ctc/GC+113/cx72f04/VVpxST5s9mk6W6nDTNt7gMy3dW2v98dD5S641YN1zSXsF3prCCW7lCdLW6lZ3m4W2b9_sK8nyD5DW3npRDc3Wp7HrW1Mny343JpRywW1vSLj83kj7m_W4c7PDN3NgV2CW3PkYy14FTBf9W67nc6y1Y4TBRN3H6_6WLh5nxW7mt_tx5WR9hsW35B6Bz9c89y5W2bSgMr54gl64W9hjwPw75YTwCW2j6cS48cBw4xN7ClHJd-qdxZW3WH3sB7-5qdQW3r8vgG4gmPSPW6Vg1Fg6MnV6-W8PkzZk45H_SzN9klrjt_LR70W3TBRdK7hSszKW7r5NdK2qlTKbW1PQsmL9fm8_1W8YHg9f7xFwkMW14SJ9L3vsS31f9gycBY04 )  Organization admins can now set a maximum lifetime for every token: personal, organization, and team. Compliance is checked on each request, and any token past the limit is rejected with a clear error, so credential rotation is enforced at the platform level.

Spotlight: Usage Limits for Pulumi Neo

Neo can plan and deploy real infrastructure on its own, and now you can put a budget around it. Set a monthly dollar limit for your organization and Neo pauses when it is reached. Add per-member limits so no single person can spend the whole pool, and get email alerts at 50, 80, 95, and 100 percent of the organization threshold. Admins and billing owners get a clear ceiling on AI agent spend without turning the agent off.

Read the announcement → (https://info.pulumi.com/e3t/Ctc/GC+113/cx72f04/VVpxST5s9mk6W6nDTNt7gMy3dW2v98dD5S641YN1zSXsl3prCCW6N1vHY6lZ3ndW4pp-sW1XhdsRW1jbSJk5fx2x4W92Wbfr5RK6CCW4fD3kl4P9Ln4W3XMryy5LQpwSW6bS13T2kKMW9W2XwbjL1lpc5dW4V8bb13d6QMXW9fNXkc6Dz2R7W8W_7Rb7sZsW2N6FywNDr-Kj0W5XbZQ_5nv-72W68xw-810nGW_VTLwtV7JvPMTN24vqQ0zv-LrW6vmLlv47TSpqN55CVBgkJd0XW8ZwDn23cTKx8VpnTyB7yzp8FW2Mj49s72BZMWVBTxtq11PnHKW6yq4_924_wTzf7gQ31q04 )

Good to Know

-

The Standalone ESC CLI Is Retiring (https://info.pulumi.com/e3t/Ctc/GC+113/cx72f04/VVpxST5s9mk6W6nDTNt7gMy3dW2v98dD5S641YN1zSXsF3prCCW7lCdLW6lZ3lSW764fDJ8HhWBRW26Shpd6l-KJdW6T63fK2snhm2W72Y2-T3mqy0cW7J_djW6JWTHFW2-y_X81FNMs9W6d1GVw83Yl4VW1_HJk_7CX3yQW7JFJfh3rl9HtW2xPJ1_3rmywNN3NZ1FnnSJ8pVgGw8Y5f6j36W7m3cK360ZRGQW2k2B4_7WdbqXW5gbpcf6pNfdXW578gLT2D0165W87w0721sQtdjW2wFksW66fMtJW5g_PR06FZJRfVZKMjV5Y1t18W8rHYV73WZKlYW2-3KbV7kN-xNV64nXV95HrSWW5QVDRH2H_dkvf6czR5204 )  The separate esc CLI has shipped its final release (v0.26.0) and now lives inside the main Pulumi CLI. email.body:
New Controls for Agents and Secrets

July 2026

Hi friend,

The last few months put AI agents at the center of Pulumi. July was about keeping them, and the secrets and credentials underneath, under control. You can now cap how much Neo spends in a month, sign in to Pulumi Cloud with a passkey, enforce a maximum lifetime on every access token, and preview an ESC change on a real stack before it ships.

Key Product Updates

-

Preview ESC Changes Before They Ship (https://info.pulumi.com/e3t/Ctc/GC+113/cx72f04/VVpxST5s9mk6W6nDTNt7gMy3dW2v98dD5S641YN1zSXsY3prCCW7Y8-PT6lZ3lHW6nsvQ85jG6yMW5m90FV8HLkdYW5GdbJg46CCJTW3R6ZX94v08qGVdvZzS5XR325W1TyVqn278WkrN2dSRSh2g6D4W84S4Td6T3KHQN1rhP7Yk091BW251n3b10h4CsW7_rZbG6NL1HfW7lxQrj3GXSG6W6JYH0t2K5x1RW6qbtdj4ymly_W5g_Rc17hFWNkW6cWlrT2nWNjcW2nDZ1X6wSCkrW4PMsfL1BVbVWN7YgsP8g7VmPW2Fnxf92y2BdBW2sQ9ng21Z39jW1hZprW8Q7srMW4bC_QP1NTGWYW7Vd7gP7bTj-JVKCC9X4jHPV4W491pCG68R6zwf5pLDWH04 )  A new --override-env flag lets you swap in a draft environment and run pulumi preview or pulumi up against it, so a reviewer can test a configuration change on a real stack before it is approved. New Controls for Agents and Secrets

July 2026

Hi friend,

The last few months put AI agents at the center of Pulumi. July was about keeping them, and the secrets and credentials underneath, under control. You can now cap how much Neo spends in a month, sign in to Pulumi Cloud with a passkey, enforce a maximum lifetime on every access token, and preview an ESC change on a real stack before it ships.

Key Product Updates

-

Preview ESC Changes Before They Ship (https://info.pulumi.com/e3t/Ctc/GC+113/cx72f04/VVpxST5s9mk6W6nDTNt7gMy3dW2v98dD5S641YN1zSXsY3prCCW7Y8-PT6lZ3lHW6nsvQ85jG6yMW5m90FV8HLkdYW5GdbJg46CCJTW3R6ZX94v08qGVdvZzS5XR325W1TyVqn278WkrN2dSRSh2g6D4W84S4Td6T3KHQN1rhP7Yk091BW251n3b10h4CsW7_rZbG6NL1HfW7lxQrj3GXSG6W6JYH0t2K5x1RW6qbtdj4ymly_W5g_Rc17hFWNkW6cWlrT2nWNjcW2nDZ1X6wSCkrW4PMsfL1BVbVWN7YgsP8g7VmPW2Fnxf92y2BdBW2sQ9ng21Z39jW1hZprW8Q7srMW4bC_QP1NTGWYW7Vd7gP7bTj-JVKCC9X4jHPV4W491pCG68R6zwf5pLDWH04 )  A new --override-env flag lets you swap in a draft environment and run pulumi preview or pulumi up against it, so a reviewer can test a configuration change on a real stack before it is approved. Reference a draft with @draft:<draft-id>, and layer several overrides at once.

-

Sign in to Pulumi Cloud with Passkeys (https://info.pulumi.com/e3t/Ctc/GC+113/cx72f04/VVpxST5s9mk6W6nDTNt7gMy3dW2v98dD5S641YN1zSXsF3prCCW7lCdLW6lZ3nBVqWmLj1rJDB0W5YrRs58Z5JhtW1BbNrm8h7l0lN2Fg7W73wzXtN70kHKznfDrnW29ZF3r2grSR3W6ZMMTG6WtTGxW3VP2xb5jtrgWW8W9ftb2kfnpvW97hv5F8KYn3qW3YZnK143Q8wjVcw-3H3ZY7L-W1zdLkL59BsshW6j-xfS8CvgTxW85NnbR8SpCMhW43d8wp6BPwvQW1lks2b4t7hMRW70kHbb69cn5dW88pZcx38DsthVPcm5S5f9rWqW5h0W3p6CbD2fN1nxJQh2Lq_0VF62K_4HldH2MLXd0TVTm69f4W8dVK04 )  Email and password users can now add a passkey and sign in with a biometric or hardware key. Passkeys bind to Pulumi's domain, so they are phishing-resistant by design and remove the shared-secret risk that comes with passwords.

-

Enforce Access Token Expiry Policies (https://info.pulumi.com/e3t/Ctc/GC+113/cx72f04/VVpxST5s9mk6W6nDTNt7gMy3dW2v98dD5S641YN1zSXsF3prCCW7lCdLW6lZ3m4W2b9_sK8nyD5DW3npRDc3Wp7HrW1Mny343JpRywW1vSLj83kj7m_W4c7PDN3NgV2CW3PkYy14FTBf9W67nc6y1Y4TBRN3H6_6WLh5nxW7mt_tx5WR9hsW35B6Bz9c89y5W2bSgMr54gl64W9hjwPw75YTwCW2j6cS48cBw4xN7ClHJd-qdxZW3WH3sB7-5qdQW3r8vgG4gmPSPW6Vg1Fg6MnV6-W8PkzZk45H_SzN9klrjt_LR70W3TBRdK7hSszKW7r5NdK2qlTKbW1PQsmL9fm8_1W8YHg9f7xFwkMW14SJ9L3vsS31f9gycBY04 )  Organization admins can now set a maximum lifetime for every token: personal, organization, and team. Compliance is checked on each request, and any token past the limit is rejected with a clear error, so credential rotation is enforced at the platform level.

Spotlight: Usage Limits for Pulumi Neo

Neo can plan and deploy real infrastructure on its own, and now you can put a budget around it. Set a monthly dollar limit for your organization and Neo pauses when it is reached. Add per-member limits so no single person can spend the whole pool, and get email alerts at 50, 80, 95, and 100 percent of the organization threshold. Admins and billing owners get a clear ceiling on AI agent spend without turning the agent off.

Hey there,

Have you ever felt that little spark when you solve a tricky Python problem?

That “aha!” moment when everything clicks?

I live for those moments, and I want to help you experience them more often...

That’s why I’m excited to offer you a full week of free access to Real Python’s membership program—no strings attached.

Imagine what you could achieve with:

* Unlimited access to our extensive library of Python tutorials and courses.
* Hands-on projects that let you apply what you learn immediately.
* Expert guidance from seasoned Python developers ready to help you succeed.

Whether you’re just starting out or looking to level up your skills, we’ve got something for you:

👉 Ready to dive in? [Click here to start your free week now!] ( https://realpython.com/account/join?o=iiif57mCdg28OEPLV3ibg&plan=trial&email=gt2oaep3@gmail.com )

I’m confident that once you see what Real Python has to offer, you’ll wonder how you ever got along without it.

Happy Pythoning!

— Dan Bader

you the best of luck and hope to be in touch soon.

The numbers behind Truth API
A new service selling early access to President Trump’s Truth Social posts has drawn plenty of controversy — and speculation about whether Wall Street firms will pay for it, Niko Gallogly reports.

Called Truth API, the product was created by Trump Media and Technology Group, Truth Social’s parent company.

Ten customers have signed up for Truth API so far, according to a person who is close to the company but not authorized to speak publicly about confidential information. They’re primarily trading firms whose algorithms can execute trades in fractions of a second.

For a monthly subscription fee between $60,000 and $100,000, the service alerts customers to Truth Social posts from influential accounts, including the president’s, milliseconds after the posts go up on Truth Social.

The numbers behind Truth API
A new service selling early access to President Trump’s Truth Social posts has drawn plenty of controversy — and speculation about whether Wall Street firms will pay for it, Niko Gallogly reports.

Called Truth API, the product was created by Trump Media and Technology Group, Truth Social’s parent company.

Ten customers have signed up for Truth API so far, according to a person who is close to the company but not authorized to speak publicly about confidential information. They’re primarily trading firms whose algorithms can execute trades in fractions of a second.

For a monthly subscription fee between $60,000 and $100,000, the service alerts customers to Truth Social posts from influential accounts, including the president’s, milliseconds after the posts go up on Truth Social.

Good morning. Andrew here. Would you pay as much as $100,000 a month to read President Trump’s posts a few milliseconds ahead of everyone else? Niko Gallogly did some digging to uncover how many trading firms have actually signed up for this data feed.

Beyond the steep price tag lies a glaring question: Should a political figure be able to profit off market-moving announcements? More below. (Was this newsletter forwarded to you? 
https://nl.nytimes.com/f/a/uYOOhB84phX9S4VM6cLDUA~~/AAAAARA~/jLP05XhgrrqXTVSMdwPttqhV8EA17oynUiWcVDDWu4gZXlhDJEccU43LUCwtmpgljGWtrgE0ERzvVhyWqITZoyrw8ZJ8nxxNAKFqH7lgp5mTIvvW_Q0GZxFr24_ozf9KPuAXw1i7cV4gjQ0Q_FJRA4YBcETWGtHF6SDurgfY400c8XP1uBjn4_MpNn_cDaKbk3UjNh-2q3BEyW3kTC96vWszPumKocb2Fh6V1M6qNmc4g7KMVsMqvmpMCD6D3m6ZHtUlM2vpiFMFDSwBN6EFBaarp4iFf92lMNVUhQsECxpyP46TNCf3k6dCfEIRASwFBDYKPrOKW_RPc9LT3G3NTQ~~ 
Sign up here. )

Demis Hassabis, center, with President Trump and President Lee Jae Myung of South Korea. He leads artificial intelligence at Google but acts as more of a statesman for the technology. Pool photo by Julia Demaree Nikhinson

Google’s A.I. future
Investors in Google panicked yesterday after the tech giant announced a 
https://nl.nytimes.com/f/newsletter/naGoBLpO8b4-RJ5fs07HaQ~~/AAAAARA~/w0rVAoaOrwJ19SGmeG3HlRoASTqk9tZtDzFZXRkKc5GwvYQsK0otNEpwSHEI16c8fwiIlTgXNY8TfiqO2py5pF2xks5IZnY7YSS3qP05S4wMrFwA1lzJvGfZqFDaeE8gbGcjEUP59nEOK8ucIeVnQnghHwDJOtPKWETnV4nvZ8ssAbl9hA8TELOXegm0vhNU7IruYTr-sjRvjQpG8mMMqG8YDm03hL7Kxe_tCVSmn3-ILLg_ynp3_aG4GbZTBCkW84DR6gatl70HC51FfStX9uVZEgYtM4dlaWMBuy1b8gokp9YrknmDB1NJtPXs1EPYylTKfExmR44tJdc-EHPA_mlyO7EuQRpk5DjfVGBwXKxVNYXnYdCngHdTY3e37MX2 
major shake-up  in the leadership of its artificial intelligence division, Google DeepMind, and the departure of a hugely influential scientist.

The impact of the changes may be less than it initially appeared. But Wall Street’s reaction reflects anxiety about whether Google can catch up to its A.I. rivals.

What’s happened:

	- Demis Hassabis, the C.E.O. of Google DeepMind, will become chair of the unit and chief scientist of Google’s parent company, Alphabet.
	- Koray Kavukcuoglu, a top lieutenant to Hassabis, will take over day-to-day management of Google DeepMind.
	- Jeff Dean, Google’s chief scientist, and three other colleagues are leaving to 
https://nl.nytimes.com/f/newsletter/1ajCK3KkAzJvvRo70RRNpg~~/AAAAARA~/Nnv4_CZfD4nAjN_OSS6AZ-XK3JwH3ZYdZJ3QA5ZroAlw6tZ0lwI1QaPwJ0ht2w_GBqmz0TNbS5ptKd0K55SdRLgEf1miCaE0UMQ9gHY_2G9o5qMXCjZIFk1Z_CtMCRsMnam6F6pS8pE4ld-3t5E-H1ONZRk4BCe96zN5pY5LKp1YKsHJLtYqT9eaC0Mha2HZxj2qt5JLijOfbkonvwz9w42yAtscxA3PqBTAr9kF_bR3PhDhkn010KPqU9PJXwT4f4WbzA22FyS4MScGk4vU3WN67_60S_vFoX7rpzEJ_veKX7khRQs9XlDHnOFuPnlD8JDu95BNH66bkxTwhkC5ryIvQF0X7TdeJS7Q75-ugpPM2e-z2gC_bGzflpFvjusL 
found an A.I. start-up .

The background:

	- Hassabis had 
https://nl.nytimes.com/f/a/JmFXVHsWLNLwOMwoYOxPtQ~~/AAAAARA~/C6wpofAK5mcr4gb5S1LpUh2pedjcqFrN-XC7X5t5HTtEbDJrzYdExBRD9aOcP8u5sWa5ZsN6sqzRkGJLI2jVMPBv679Wu08fI2NrpwfN6QY1paCmUzM7XfpEDfcRBijh8F-WeB_OBLI_N4hFfr5YcwrIu0FDGquL-4wpNmRszI47P5wUaMVrWfqF9F8bPs2xKFKAmlbLlE4ZCZMhaRr6LHhLwxhZEdVufgeWp5S3VFikFpcaddtrZKzK3VTvYaXNeVjpmx7VhZiNVD5KShAcuOGkppZtAfo0xoKkdlnFo2lgwzivJaW8tjbxdmKHA54OXTOplj-G5svkVRcGNfjSNgs9V4cV6eq8tcX6UQrlbaQOIxF-VT3e2Py0qADQTdUy_FlIdFqHt12dHLr48sKbDJD4l8fQfzj4bh9lI1oVn9Q~ 
already been delegating  day-to-day management of Google DeepMind to Kavukcuoglu, according to Semafor.
	- Dean, though revered by many Google engineers and one of the company’s earliest hires, hadn’t been at the forefront of the company’s A.I. efforts. (Sergey Brin, a Google founder, has been increasingly hands-on.) In a sign of apparent comity, Google will invest in Dean’s new start-up.

Hassabis has become one of the company’s statesmen on A.I. — he was Google’s representative at the A.I.-focused Group of 7 meeting this summer — and is increasingly focused on issues like the technology’s social impact. (He also runs 
https://nl.nytimes.com/f/newsletter/wrB2KY2HHqcwRhwrmDQ0LA~~/AAAAARA~/xsE3Swcmy7c_dSgU1Eb92AcgyXSYQ9DGTyu94daFcx9aehcryWDTS01CfY3nL2_f46f0PDMGvWifBhn3v-pcH31fJZJBcvgBoDSXoZLe205WkfbcRQ_ohLbGyH5vjzwQ2FjtjIEFaxvSZmwvjVz8vPjNs31JHABVCiJu2zXLSgOcL4jTYj20Lgx0BTNV2d_qpQFkqC2dYkwkqNX2pLS8iHFC4XEktV59zDvPu8zgGPbmtXxCjFTCZN8GhR5IEMG0LdXBQjJVcsJQsuHs9LLw6baN-q_D9dBURRk7l6psolc31J3D5s2B2_6FZEhaS2nxOqhkx6mzF7E1bdkCtRu0jkhrFlanWlbeulaU9GldAxv5i_7LUUUZBNJa72-xW3LWNwVGY7DPPCVSf92D5SUNHA~~ 
Isomorphic Labs , an A.I.-focused drug discovery start-up spun out of Google.)

The bigger issue: Google is an A.I. also-ran. Yes, it has successfully inserted its Gemini technology into its vast suite of products. It also won plaudits when its Gemini 3 model was released in November.

But its models are now considered several steps behind cutting-edge rivals from Anthropic and OpenAI. (It still hasn’t released its high-end Gemini 3.5 Pro model.)

The numbers behind Truth API
A new service selling early access to President Trump’s Truth Social posts has drawn plenty of controversy — and speculation about whether Wall Street firms will pay for it, Niko Gallogly reports.

Called Truth API, the product was created by Trump Media and Technology Group, Truth Social’s parent company.

Ten customers have signed up for Truth API so far, according to a person who is close to the company but not authorized to speak publicly about confidential information. They’re primarily trading firms whose algorithms can execute trades in fractions of a second.

For a monthly subscription fee between $60,000 and $100,000, the service alerts customers to Truth Social posts from influential accounts, including the president’s, milliseconds after the posts go up on Truth Social.

The numbers behind Truth API
A new service selling early access to President Trump’s Truth Social posts has drawn plenty of controversy — and speculation about whether Wall Street firms will pay for it, Niko Gallogly reports.

Called Truth API, the product was created by Trump Media and Technology Group, Truth Social’s parent company.

Ten customers have signed up for Truth API so far, according to a person who is close to the company but not authorized to speak publicly about confidential information. They’re primarily trading firms whose algorithms can execute trades in fractions of a second.

For a monthly subscription fee between $60,000 and $100,000, the service alerts customers to Truth Social posts from influential accounts, including the president’s, milliseconds after the posts go up on Truth Social.

The numbers behind Truth API
A new service selling early access to President Trump’s Truth Social posts has drawn plenty of controversy — and speculation about whether Wall Street firms will pay for it, Niko Gallogly reports.

Called Truth API, the product was created by Trump Media and Technology Group, Truth Social’s parent company.

Ten customers have signed up for Truth API so far, according to a person who is close to the company but not authorized to speak publicly about confidential information. They’re primarily trading firms whose algorithms can execute trades in fractions of a second.

For a monthly subscription fee between $60,000 and $100,000, the service alerts customers to Truth Social posts from influential accounts, including the president’s, milliseconds after the posts go up on Truth Social.

Good morning. Andrew here. Would you pay as much as $100,000 a month to read President Trump’s posts a few milliseconds ahead of everyone else? Niko Gallogly did some digging to uncover how many trading firms have actually signed up for this data feed.

Beyond the steep price tag lies a glaring question: Should a political figure be able to profit off market-moving announcements? More below. (Was this newsletter forwarded to you? 
https://nl.nytimes.com/f/a/uYOOhB84phX9S4VM6cLDUA~~/AAAAARA~/jLP05XhgrrqXTVSMdwPttqhV8EA17oynUiWcVDDWu4gZXlhDJEccU43LUCwtmpgljGWtrgE0ERzvVhyWqITZoyrw8ZJ8nxxNAKFqH7lgp5mTIvvW_Q0GZxFr24_ozf9KPuAXw1i7cV4gjQ0Q_FJRA4YBcETWGtHF6SDurgfY400c8XP1uBjn4_MpNn_cDaKbk3UjNh-2q3BEyW3kTC96vWszPumKocb2Fh6V1M6qNmc4g7KMVsMqvmpMCD6D3m6ZHtUlM2vpiFMFDSwBN6EFBaarp4iFf92lMNVUhQsECxpyP46TNCf3k6dCfEIRASwFBDYKPrOKW_RPc9LT3G3NTQ~~ 
Sign up here. )

Demis Hassabis, center, with President Trump and President Lee Jae Myung of South Korea. He leads artificial intelligence at Google but acts as more of a statesman for the technology. Pool photo by Julia Demaree Nikhinson

Google’s A.I. future
Investors in Google panicked yesterday after the tech giant announced a 
https://nl.nytimes.com/f/newsletter/naGoBLpO8b4-RJ5fs07HaQ~~/AAAAARA~/w0rVAoaOrwJ19SGmeG3HlRoASTqk9tZtDzFZXRkKc5GwvYQsK0otNEpwSHEI16c8fwiIlTgXNY8TfiqO2py5pF2xks5IZnY7YSS3qP05S4wMrFwA1lzJvGfZqFDaeE8gbGcjEUP59nEOK8ucIeVnQnghHwDJOtPKWETnV4nvZ8ssAbl9hA8TELOXegm0vhNU7IruYTr-sjRvjQpG8mMMqG8YDm03hL7Kxe_tCVSmn3-ILLg_ynp3_aG4GbZTBCkW84DR6gatl70HC51FfStX9uVZEgYtM4dlaWMBuy1b8gokp9YrknmDB1NJtPXs1EPYylTKfExmR44tJdc-EHPA_mlyO7EuQRpk5DjfVGBwXKxVNYXnYdCngHdTY3e37MX2 
major shake-up  in the leadership of its artificial intelligence division, Google DeepMind, and the departure of a hugely influential scientist.

The impact of the changes may be less than it initially appeared. But Wall Street’s reaction reflects anxiety about whether Google can catch up to its A.I. rivals.

What’s happened:

	- Demis Hassabis, the C.E.O. of Google DeepMind, will become chair of the unit and chief scientist of Google’s parent company, Alphabet.
	- Koray Kavukcuoglu, a top lieutenant to Hassabis, will take over day-to-day management of Google DeepMind.
	- Jeff Dean, Google’s chief scientist, and three other colleagues are leaving to 
https://nl.nytimes.com/f/newsletter/1ajCK3KkAzJvvRo70RRNpg~~/AAAAARA~/Nnv4_CZfD4nAjN_OSS6AZ-XK3JwH3ZYdZJ3QA5ZroAlw6tZ0lwI1QaPwJ0ht2w_GBqmz0TNbS5ptKd0K55SdRLgEf1miCaE0UMQ9gHY_2G9o5qMXCjZIFk1Z_CtMCRsMnam6F6pS8pE4ld-3t5E-H1ONZRk4BCe96zN5pY5LKp1YKsHJLtYqT9eaC0Mha2HZxj2qt5JLijOfbkonvwz9w42yAtscxA3PqBTAr9kF_bR3PhDhkn010KPqU9PJXwT4f4WbzA22FyS4MScGk4vU3WN67_60S_vFoX7rpzEJ_veKX7khRQs9XlDHnOFuPnlD8JDu95BNH66bkxTwhkC5ryIvQF0X7TdeJS7Q75-ugpPM2e-z2gC_bGzflpFvjusL 
found an A.I. start-up .

The background:

	- Hassabis had 
https://nl.nytimes.com/f/a/JmFXVHsWLNLwOMwoYOxPtQ~~/AAAAARA~/C6wpofAK5mcr4gb5S1LpUh2pedjcqFrN-XC7X5t5HTtEbDJrzYdExBRD9aOcP8u5sWa5ZsN6sqzRkGJLI2jVMPBv679Wu08fI2NrpwfN6QY1paCmUzM7XfpEDfcRBijh8F-WeB_OBLI_N4hFfr5YcwrIu0FDGquL-4wpNmRszI47P5wUaMVrWfqF9F8bPs2xKFKAmlbLlE4ZCZMhaRr6LHhLwxhZEdVufgeWp5S3VFikFpcaddtrZKzK3VTvYaXNeVjpmx7VhZiNVD5KShAcuOGkppZtAfo0xoKkdlnFo2lgwzivJaW8tjbxdmKHA54OXTOplj-G5svkVRcGNfjSNgs9V4cV6eq8tcX6UQrlbaQOIxF-VT3e2Py0qADQTdUy_FlIdFqHt12dHLr48sKbDJD4l8fQfzj4bh9lI1oVn9Q~ 
already been delegating  day-to-day management of Google DeepMind to Kavukcuoglu, according to Semafor.
	- Dean, though revered by many Google engineers and one of the company’s earliest hires, hadn’t been at the forefront of the company’s A.I. efforts. (Sergey Brin, a Google founder, has been increasingly hands-on.) In a sign of apparent comity, Google will invest in Dean’s new start-up.

Hassabis has become one of the company’s statesmen on A.I. — he was Google’s representative at the A.I.-focused Group of 7 meeting this summer — and is increasingly focused on issues like the technology’s social impact. (He also runs 
https://nl.nytimes.com/f/newsletter/wrB2KY2HHqcwRhwrmDQ0LA~~/AAAAARA~/xsE3Swcmy7c_dSgU1Eb92AcgyXSYQ9DGTyu94daFcx9aehcryWDTS01CfY3nL2_f46f0PDMGvWifBhn3v-pcH31fJZJBcvgBoDSXoZLe205WkfbcRQ_ohLbGyH5vjzwQ2FjtjIEFaxvSZmwvjVz8vPjNs31JHABVCiJu2zXLSgOcL4jTYj20Lgx0BTNV2d_qpQFkqC2dYkwkqNX2pLS8iHFC4XEktV59zDvPu8zgGPbmtXxCjFTCZN8GhR5IEMG0LdXBQjJVcsJQsuHs9LLw6baN-q_D9dBURRk7l6psolc31J3D5s2B2_6FZEhaS2nxOqhkx6mzF7E1bdkCtRu0jkhrFlanWlbeulaU9GldAxv5i_7LUUUZBNJa72-xW3LWNwVGY7DPPCVSf92D5SUNHA~~ 
Isomorphic Labs , an A.I.-focused drug discovery start-up spun out of Google.)

The bigger issue: Google is an A.I. also-ran. Yes, it has successfully inserted its Gemini technology into its vast suite of products. It also won plaudits when its Gemini 3 model was released in November.

But its models are now considered several steps behind cutting-edge rivals from Anthropic and OpenAI. (It still hasn’t released its high-end Gemini 3.5 Pro model.)

The numbers behind Truth API
A new service selling early access to President Trump’s Truth Social posts has drawn plenty of controversy — and speculation about whether Wall Street firms will pay for it, Niko Gallogly reports.

Called Truth API, the product was created by Trump Media and Technology Group, Truth Social’s parent company.

Ten customers have signed up for Truth API so far, according to a person who is close to the company but not authorized to speak publicly about confidential information. They’re primarily trading firms whose algorithms can execute trades in fractions of a second.

For a monthly subscription fee between $60,000 and $100,000, the service alerts customers to Truth Social posts from influential accounts, including the president’s, milliseconds after the posts go up on Truth Social.

The numbers behind Truth API
A new service selling early access to President Trump’s Truth Social posts has drawn plenty of controversy — and speculation about whether Wall Street firms will pay for it, Niko Gallogly reports.

Called Truth API, the product was created by Trump Media and Technology Group, Truth Social’s parent company.

Ten customers have signed up for Truth API so far, according to a person who is close to the company but not authorized to speak publicly about confidential information. They’re primarily trading firms whose algorithms can execute trades in fractions of a second.

For a monthly subscription fee between $60,000 and $100,000, the service alerts customers to Truth Social posts from influential accounts, including the president’s, milliseconds after the posts go up on Truth Social.

The numbers behind Truth API
A new service selling early access to President Trump’s Truth Social posts has drawn plenty of controversy — and speculation about whether Wall Street firms will pay for it, Niko Gallogly reports.

Called Truth API, the product was created by Trump Media and Technology Group, Truth Social’s parent company.

Ten customers have signed up for Truth API so far, according to a person who is close to the company but not authorized to speak publicly about confidential information. They’re primarily trading firms whose algorithms can execute trades in fractions of a second.

For a monthly subscription fee between $60,000 and $100,000, the service alerts customers to Truth Social posts from influential accounts, including the president’s, milliseconds after the posts go up on Truth Social.

Good morning. Andrew here. Would you pay as much as $100,000 a month to read President Trump’s posts a few milliseconds ahead of everyone else? Niko Gallogly did some digging to uncover how many trading firms have actually signed up for this data feed.

Beyond the steep price tag lies a glaring question: Should a political figure be able to profit off market-moving announcements? More below. (Was this newsletter forwarded to you? 
https://nl.nytimes.com/f/a/uYOOhB84phX9S4VM6cLDUA~~/AAAAARA~/jLP05XhgrrqXTVSMdwPttqhV8EA17oynUiWcVDDWu4gZXlhDJEccU43LUCwtmpgljGWtrgE0ERzvVhyWqITZoyrw8ZJ8nxxNAKFqH7lgp5mTIvvW_Q0GZxFr24_ozf9KPuAXw1i7cV4gjQ0Q_FJRA4YBcETWGtHF6SDurgfY400c8XP1uBjn4_MpNn_cDaKbk3UjNh-2q3BEyW3kTC96vWszPumKocb2Fh6V1M6qNmc4g7KMVsMqvmpMCD6D3m6ZHtUlM2vpiFMFDSwBN6EFBaarp4iFf92lMNVUhQsECxpyP46TNCf3k6dCfEIRASwFBDYKPrOKW_RPc9LT3G3NTQ~~ 
Sign up here. )

Demis Hassabis, center, with President Trump and President Lee Jae Myung of South Korea. He leads artificial intelligence at Google but acts as more of a statesman for the technology. Pool photo by Julia Demaree Nikhinson

Google’s A.I. future
Investors in Google panicked yesterday after the tech giant announced a 
https://nl.nytimes.com/f/newsletter/naGoBLpO8b4-RJ5fs07HaQ~~/AAAAARA~/w0rVAoaOrwJ19SGmeG3HlRoASTqk9tZtDzFZXRkKc5GwvYQsK0otNEpwSHEI16c8fwiIlTgXNY8TfiqO2py5pF2xks5IZnY7YSS3qP05S4wMrFwA1lzJvGfZqFDaeE8gbGcjEUP59nEOK8ucIeVnQnghHwDJOtPKWETnV4nvZ8ssAbl9hA8TELOXegm0vhNU7IruYTr-sjRvjQpG8mMMqG8YDm03hL7Kxe_tCVSmn3-ILLg_ynp3_aG4GbZTBCkW84DR6gatl70HC51FfStX9uVZEgYtM4dlaWMBuy1b8gokp9YrknmDB1NJtPXs1EPYylTKfExmR44tJdc-EHPA_mlyO7EuQRpk5DjfVGBwXKxVNYXnYdCngHdTY3e37MX2 
major shake-up  in the leadership of its artificial intelligence division, Google DeepMind, and the departure of a hugely influential scientist.

The impact of the changes may be less than it initially appeared. But Wall Street’s reaction reflects anxiety about whether Google can catch up to its A.I. rivals.

What’s happened:

	- Demis Hassabis, the C.E.O. of Google DeepMind, will become chair of the unit and chief scientist of Google’s parent company, Alphabet.
	- Koray Kavukcuoglu, a top lieutenant to Hassabis, will take over day-to-day management of Google DeepMind.
	- Jeff Dean, Google’s chief scientist, and three other colleagues are leaving to 
https://nl.nytimes.com/f/newsletter/1ajCK3KkAzJvvRo70RRNpg~~/AAAAARA~/Nnv4_CZfD4nAjN_OSS6AZ-XK3JwH3ZYdZJ3QA5ZroAlw6tZ0lwI1QaPwJ0ht2w_GBqmz0TNbS5ptKd0K55SdRLgEf1miCaE0UMQ9gHY_2G9o5qMXCjZIFk1Z_CtMCRsMnam6F6pS8pE4ld-3t5E-H1ONZRk4BCe96zN5pY5LKp1YKsHJLtYqT9eaC0Mha2HZxj2qt5JLijOfbkonvwz9w42yAtscxA3PqBTAr9kF_bR3PhDhkn010KPqU9PJXwT4f4WbzA22FyS4MScGk4vU3WN67_60S_vFoX7rpzEJ_veKX7khRQs9XlDHnOFuPnlD8JDu95BNH66bkxTwhkC5ryIvQF0X7TdeJS7Q75-ugpPM2e-z2gC_bGzflpFvjusL 
found an A.I. start-up .

The background:

	- Hassabis had 
https://nl.nytimes.com/f/a/JmFXVHsWLNLwOMwoYOxPtQ~~/AAAAARA~/C6wpofAK5mcr4gb5S1LpUh2pedjcqFrN-XC7X5t5HTtEbDJrzYdExBRD9aOcP8u5sWa5ZsN6sqzRkGJLI2jVMPBv679Wu08fI2NrpwfN6QY1paCmUzM7XfpEDfcRBijh8F-WeB_OBLI_N4hFfr5YcwrIu0FDGquL-4wpNmRszI47P5wUaMVrWfqF9F8bPs2xKFKAmlbLlE4ZCZMhaRr6LHhLwxhZEdVufgeWp5S3VFikFpcaddtrZKzK3VTvYaXNeVjpmx7VhZiNVD5KShAcuOGkppZtAfo0xoKkdlnFo2lgwzivJaW8tjbxdmKHA54OXTOplj-G5svkVRcGNfjSNgs9V4cV6eq8tcX6UQrlbaQOIxF-VT3e2Py0qADQTdUy_FlIdFqHt12dHLr48sKbDJD4l8fQfzj4bh9lI1oVn9Q~ 
already been delegating  day-to-day management of Google DeepMind to Kavukcuoglu, according to Semafor.
	- Dean, though revered by many Google engineers and one of the company’s earliest hires, hadn’t been at the forefront of the company’s A.I. efforts. (Sergey Brin, a Google founder, has been increasingly hands-on.) In a sign of apparent comity, Google will invest in Dean’s new start-up.

Hassabis has become one of the company’s statesmen on A.I. — he was Google’s representative at the A.I.-focused Group of 7 meeting this summer — and is increasingly focused on issues like the technology’s social impact. (He also runs 
https://nl.nytimes.com/f/newsletter/wrB2KY2HHqcwRhwrmDQ0LA~~/AAAAARA~/xsE3Swcmy7c_dSgU1Eb92AcgyXSYQ9DGTyu94daFcx9aehcryWDTS01CfY3nL2_f46f0PDMGvWifBhn3v-pcH31fJZJBcvgBoDSXoZLe205WkfbcRQ_ohLbGyH5vjzwQ2FjtjIEFaxvSZmwvjVz8vPjNs31JHABVCiJu2zXLSgOcL4jTYj20Lgx0BTNV2d_qpQFkqC2dYkwkqNX2pLS8iHFC4XEktV59zDvPu8zgGPbmtXxCjFTCZN8GhR5IEMG0LdXBQjJVcsJQsuHs9LLw6baN-q_D9dBURRk7l6psolc31J3D5s2B2_6FZEhaS2nxOqhkx6mzF7E1bdkCtRu0jkhrFlanWlbeulaU9GldAxv5i_7LUUUZBNJa72-xW3LWNwVGY7DPPCVSf92D5SUNHA~~ 
Isomorphic Labs , an A.I.-focused drug discovery start-up spun out of Google.)

The bigger issue: Google is an A.I. also-ran. Yes, it has successfully inserted its Gemini technology into its vast suite of products. It also won plaudits when its Gemini 3 model was released in November.

But its models are now considered several steps behind cutting-edge rivals from Anthropic and OpenAI. (It still hasn’t released its high-end Gemini 3.5 Pro model.)

The numbers behind Truth API
A new service selling early access to President Trump’s Truth Social posts has drawn plenty of controversy — and speculation about whether Wall Street firms will pay for it, Niko Gallogly reports.

Called Truth API, the product was created by Trump Media and Technology Group, Truth Social’s parent company.

Ten customers have signed up for Truth API so far, according to a person who is close to the company but not authorized to speak publicly about confidential information. They’re primarily trading firms whose algorithms can execute trades in fractions of a second.

For a monthly subscription fee between $60,000 and $100,000, the service alerts customers to Truth Social posts from influential accounts, including the president’s, milliseconds after the posts go up on Truth Social.

Hi Ellis,

Good morning!

Thank you for following up, and I appreciate the time and effort you invested in the interview process.

I did receive feedback from Joe. Overall, the he felt that you brought strong experience and performed well during the interview. Joe noted that you have a solid overall background and a broad range of relevant experience. However, for this particular role, they decided to move forward with a candidate whose experience aligned more closely with the specific day-to-day responsibilities and technical details of the position.

Thank you again for your interest, and I wish you the best in your continued job search. I'll certainly keep you in mind for future opportunities that may be a better match for your background.

Thank You
Avinash

Google’s A.I. future
Investors in Google panicked yesterday after the tech giant announced a 
https://nl.nytimes.com/f/newsletter/naGoBLpO8b4-RJ5fs07HaQ~~/AAAAARA~/w0rVAoaOrwJ19SGmeG3HlRoASTqk9tZtDzFZXRkKc5GwvYQsK0otNEpwSHEI16c8fwiIlTgXNY8TfiqO2py5pF2xks5IZnY7YSS3qP05S4wMrFwA1lzJvGfZqFDaeE8gbGcjEUP59nEOK8ucIeVnQnghHwDJOtPKWETnV4nvZ8ssAbl9hA8TELOXegm0vhNU7IruYTr-sjRvjQpG8mMMqG8YDm03hL7Kxe_tCVSmn3-ILLg_ynp3_aG4GbZTBCkW84DR6gatl70HC51FfStX9uVZEgYtM4dlaWMBuy1b8gokp9YrknmDB1NJtPXs1EPYylTKfExmR44tJdc-EHPA_mlyO7EuQRpk5DjfVGBwXKxVNYXnYdCngHdTY3e37MX2 
major shake-up  in the leadership of its artificial intelligence division, Google DeepMind, and the departure of a hugely influential scientist.

The impact of the changes may be less than it initially appeared. But Wall Street’s reaction reflects anxiety about whether Google can catch up to its A.I. rivals.

What’s happened:

	- Demis Hassabis, the C.E.O. of Google DeepMind, will become chair of the unit and chief scientist of Google’s parent company, Alphabet.
	- Koray Kavukcuoglu, a top lieutenant to Hassabis, will take over day-to-day management of Google DeepMind.
	- Jeff Dean, Google’s chief scientist, and three other colleagues are leaving to 
https://nl.nytimes.com/f/newsletter/1ajCK3KkAzJvvRo70RRNpg~~/AAAAARA~/Nnv4_CZfD4nAjN_OSS6AZ-XK3JwH3ZYdZJ3QA5ZroAlw6tZ0lwI1QaPwJ0ht2w_GBqmz0TNbS5ptKd0K55SdRLgEf1miCaE0UMQ9gHY_2G9o5qMXCjZIFk1Z_CtMCRsMnam6F6pS8pE4ld-3t5E-H1ONZRk4BCe96zN5pY5LKp1YKsHJLtYqT9eaC0Mha2HZxj2qt5JLijOfbkonvwz9w42yAtscxA3PqBTAr9kF_bR3PhDhkn010KPqU9PJXwT4f4WbzA22FyS4MScGk4vU3WN67_60S_vFoX7rpzEJ_veKX7khRQs9XlDHnOFuPnlD8JDu95BNH66bkxTwhkC5ryIvQF0X7TdeJS7Q75-ugpPM2e-z2gC_bGzflpFvjusL 
found an A.I. start-up .

The background:

	- Hassabis had 
https://nl.nytimes.com/f/a/JmFXVHsWLNLwOMwoYOxPtQ~~/AAAAARA~/C6wpofAK5mcr4gb5S1LpUh2pedjcqFrN-XC7X5t5HTtEbDJrzYdExBRD9aOcP8u5sWa5ZsN6sqzRkGJLI2jVMPBv679Wu08fI2NrpwfN6QY1paCmUzM7XfpEDfcRBijh8F-WeB_OBLI_N4hFfr5YcwrIu0FDGquL-4wpNmRszI47P5wUaMVrWfqF9F8bPs2xKFKAmlbLlE4ZCZMhaRr6LHhLwxhZEdVufgeWp5S3VFikFpcaddtrZKzK3VTvYaXNeVjpmx7VhZiNVD5KShAcuOGkppZtAfo0xoKkdlnFo2lgwzivJaW8tjbxdmKHA54OXTOplj-G5svkVRcGNfjSNgs9V4cV6eq8tcX6UQrlbaQOIxF-VT3e2Py0qADQTdUy_FlIdFqHt12dHLr48sKbDJD4l8fQfzj4bh9lI1oVn9Q~ 
already been delegating  day-to-day management of Google DeepMind to Kavukcuoglu, according to Semafor.
	- Dean, though revered by many Google engineers and one of the company’s earliest hires, hadn’t been at the forefront of the company’s A.I. efforts. (Sergey Brin, a Google founder, has been increasingly hands-on.) In a sign of apparent comity, Google will invest in Dean’s new start-up.

Hassabis has become one of the company’s statesmen on A.I. — he was Google’s representative at the A.I.-focused Group of 7 meeting this summer — and is increasingly focused on issues like the technology’s social impact. (He also runs 
https://nl.nytimes.com/f/newsletter/wrB2KY2HHqcwRhwrmDQ0LA~~/AAAAARA~/xsE3Swcmy7c_dSgU1Eb92AcgyXSYQ9DGTyu94daFcx9aehcryWDTS01CfY3nL2_f46f0PDMGvWifBhn3v-pcH31fJZJBcvgBoDSXoZLe205WkfbcRQ_ohLbGyH5vjzwQ2FjtjIEFaxvSZmwvjVz8vPjNs31JHABVCiJu2zXLSgOcL4jTYj20Lgx0BTNV2d_qpQFkqC2dYkwkqNX2pLS8iHFC4XEktV59zDvPu8zgGPbmtXxCjFTCZN8GhR5IEMG0LdXBQjJVcsJQsuHs9LLw6baN-q_D9dBURRk7l6psolc31J3D5s2B2_6FZEhaS2nxOqhkx6mzF7E1bdkCtRu0jkhrFlanWlbeulaU9GldAxv5i_7LUUUZBNJa72-xW3LWNwVGY7DPPCVSf92D5SUNHA~~ 
Isomorphic Labs , an A.I.-focused drug discovery start-up spun out of Google.)

The bigger issue: Google is an A.I. also-ran. Yes, it has successfully inserted its Gemini technology into its vast suite of products. It also won plaudits when its Gemini 3 model was released in November.

But its models are now considered several steps behind cutting-edge rivals from Anthropic and OpenAI. (It still hasn’t released its high-end Gemini 3.5 Pro model.)

Meanwhile, Google has continued to bleed research talent, including Noam Shazeer (to OpenAI), John Jumper (to Anthropic) and David Silver (who founded Ineffable Intelligence).

	- Google has 
https://nl.nytimes.com/f/a/vHUumBwJXtEmn8AfVtXTSA~~/AAAAARA~/3svSUtxl9_bEurP-cRrJKjxMnU9flki68IcuoeQxujQ2AwbVrB9-wEg9ieLTwncDzcqbCbpvQeUonm0BCaTTnA577iph0M9Anw4hRhKvymsshjyx6U_pndCfB3IMEcMSnZyXgipPdK0_8yKf1S-ABrxRA3DwhamhelBHqv7PYZhyuEZhmpz6I02grf7KXJTF-vsFed0iei5PTUYfJ6757siqUYoFozCElu1_j9ioKrDWz1ttVCb-Z3-49IptyzTpHnhqMP3w3Zjawg5K2lu9u3G4F4ddGKDK9ix6l_Pimy9UFWk4akGI09dLJpfhgOnfnCkZw13az7ix681Pkm_HZ6JR9QTrdVb2rfKF589rDCE~ 
revamped its research division  and formed an internal team focused on improving its models’ coding abilities, according to The Financial Times.

$195 billion to $205 billion  on capital expenditures (mostly A.I.-focused) this year, more than double what it did last year, and reported negative free cash flow for the first time since its I.P.O. in 2004.

The numbers behind Truth API
A new service selling early access to President Trump’s Truth Social posts has drawn plenty of controversy — and speculation about whether Wall Street firms will pay for it, Niko Gallogly reports.

Called Truth API, the product was created by Trump Media and Technology Group, Truth Social’s parent company.

Ten customers have signed up for Truth API so far, according to a person who is close to the company but not authorized to speak publicly about confidential information. They’re primarily trading firms whose algorithms can execute trades in fractions of a second.

For a monthly subscription fee between $60,000 and $100,000, the service alerts customers to Truth Social posts from influential accounts, including the president’s, milliseconds after the posts go up on Truth Social.

The numbers behind Truth API
A new service selling early access to President Trump’s Truth Social posts has drawn plenty of controversy — and speculation about whether Wall Street firms will pay for it, Niko Gallogly reports.

Called Truth API, the product was created by Trump Media and Technology Group, Truth Social’s parent company.

Ten customers have signed up for Truth API so far, according to a person who is close to the company but not authorized to speak publicly about confidential information. They’re primarily trading firms whose algorithms can execute trades in fractions of a second.

For a monthly subscription fee between $60,000 and $100,000, the service alerts customers to Truth Social posts from influential accounts, including the president’s, milliseconds after the posts go up on Truth Social.

Good morning. Andrew here. Would you pay as much as $100,000 a month to read President Trump’s posts a few milliseconds ahead of everyone else? Niko Gallogly did some digging to uncover how many trading firms have actually signed up for this data feed.

Beyond the steep price tag lies a glaring question: Should a political figure be able to profit off market-moving announcements? More below. (Was this newsletter forwarded to you? 
https://nl.nytimes.com/f/a/uYOOhB84phX9S4VM6cLDUA~~/AAAAARA~/jLP05XhgrrqXTVSMdwPttqhV8EA17oynUiWcVDDWu4gZXlhDJEccU43LUCwtmpgljGWtrgE0ERzvVhyWqITZoyrw8ZJ8nxxNAKFqH7lgp5mTIvvW_Q0GZxFr24_ozf9KPuAXw1i7cV4gjQ0Q_FJRA4YBcETWGtHF6SDurgfY400c8XP1uBjn4_MpNn_cDaKbk3UjNh-2q3BEyW3kTC96vWszPumKocb2Fh6V1M6qNmc4g7KMVsMqvmpMCD6D3m6ZHtUlM2vpiFMFDSwBN6EFBaarp4iFf92lMNVUhQsECxpyP46TNCf3k6dCfEIRASwFBDYKPrOKW_RPc9LT3G3NTQ~~ 
Sign up here. )

Demis Hassabis, center, with President Trump and President Lee Jae Myung of South Korea. He leads artificial intelligence at Google but acts as more of a statesman for the technology. Pool photo by Julia Demaree Nikhinson

Google’s A.I. future
Investors in Google panicked yesterday after the tech giant announced a 
https://nl.nytimes.com/f/newsletter/naGoBLpO8b4-RJ5fs07HaQ~~/AAAAARA~/w0rVAoaOrwJ19SGmeG3HlRoASTqk9tZtDzFZXRkKc5GwvYQsK0otNEpwSHEI16c8fwiIlTgXNY8TfiqO2py5pF2xks5IZnY7YSS3qP05S4wMrFwA1lzJvGfZqFDaeE8gbGcjEUP59nEOK8ucIeVnQnghHwDJOtPKWETnV4nvZ8ssAbl9hA8TELOXegm0vhNU7IruYTr-sjRvjQpG8mMMqG8YDm03hL7Kxe_tCVSmn3-ILLg_ynp3_aG4GbZTBCkW84DR6gatl70HC51FfStX9uVZEgYtM4dlaWMBuy1b8gokp9YrknmDB1NJtPXs1EPYylTKfExmR44tJdc-EHPA_mlyO7EuQRpk5DjfVGBwXKxVNYXnYdCngHdTY3e37MX2 
major shake-up  in the leadership of its artificial intelligence division, Google DeepMind, and the departure of a hugely influential scientist.

The impact of the changes may be less than it initially appeared. But Wall Street’s reaction reflects anxiety about whether Google can catch up to its A.I. rivals.

What’s happened:

	- Demis Hassabis, the C.E.O. of Google DeepMind, will become chair of the unit and chief scientist of Google’s parent company, Alphabet.
	- Koray Kavukcuoglu, a top lieutenant to Hassabis, will take over day-to-day management of Google DeepMind.
	- Jeff Dean, Google’s chief scientist, and three other colleagues are leaving to 
https://nl.nytimes.com/f/newsletter/1ajCK3KkAzJvvRo70RRNpg~~/AAAAARA~/Nnv4_CZfD4nAjN_OSS6AZ-XK3JwH3ZYdZJ3QA5ZroAlw6tZ0lwI1QaPwJ0ht2w_GBqmz0TNbS5ptKd0K55SdRLgEf1miCaE0UMQ9gHY_2G9o5qMXCjZIFk1Z_CtMCRsMnam6F6pS8pE4ld-3t5E-H1ONZRk4BCe96zN5pY5LKp1YKsHJLtYqT9eaC0Mha2HZxj2qt5JLijOfbkonvwz9w42yAtscxA3PqBTAr9kF_bR3PhDhkn010KPqU9PJXwT4f4WbzA22FyS4MScGk4vU3WN67_60S_vFoX7rpzEJ_veKX7khRQs9XlDHnOFuPnlD8JDu95BNH66bkxTwhkC5ryIvQF0X7TdeJS7Q75-ugpPM2e-z2gC_bGzflpFvjusL 
found an A.I. start-up .

The background:

	- Hassabis had 
https://nl.nytimes.com/f/a/JmFXVHsWLNLwOMwoYOxPtQ~~/AAAAARA~/C6wpofAK5mcr4gb5S1LpUh2pedjcqFrN-XC7X5t5HTtEbDJrzYdExBRD9aOcP8u5sWa5ZsN6sqzRkGJLI2jVMPBv679Wu08fI2NrpwfN6QY1paCmUzM7XfpEDfcRBijh8F-WeB_OBLI_N4hFfr5YcwrIu0FDGquL-4wpNmRszI47P5wUaMVrWfqF9F8bPs2xKFKAmlbLlE4ZCZMhaRr6LHhLwxhZEdVufgeWp5S3VFikFpcaddtrZKzK3VTvYaXNeVjpmx7VhZiNVD5KShAcuOGkppZtAfo0xoKkdlnFo2lgwzivJaW8tjbxdmKHA54OXTOplj-G5svkVRcGNfjSNgs9V4cV6eq8tcX6UQrlbaQOIxF-VT3e2Py0qADQTdUy_FlIdFqHt12dHLr48sKbDJD4l8fQfzj4bh9lI1oVn9Q~ 
already been delegating  day-to-day management of Google DeepMind to Kavukcuoglu, according to Semafor.
	- Dean, though revered by many Google engineers and one of the company’s earliest hires, hadn’t been at the forefront of the company’s A.I. efforts. (Sergey Brin, a Google founder, has been increasingly hands-on.) In a sign of apparent comity, Google will invest in Dean’s new start-up.

Hassabis has become one of the company’s statesmen on A.I. — he was Google’s representative at the A.I.-focused Group of 7 meeting this summer — and is increasingly focused on issues like the technology’s social impact. (He also runs 
https://nl.nytimes.com/f/newsletter/wrB2KY2HHqcwRhwrmDQ0LA~~/AAAAARA~/xsE3Swcmy7c_dSgU1Eb92AcgyXSYQ9DGTyu94daFcx9aehcryWDTS01CfY3nL2_f46f0PDMGvWifBhn3v-pcH31fJZJBcvgBoDSXoZLe205WkfbcRQ_ohLbGyH5vjzwQ2FjtjIEFaxvSZmwvjVz8vPjNs31JHABVCiJu2zXLSgOcL4jTYj20Lgx0BTNV2d_qpQFkqC2dYkwkqNX2pLS8iHFC4XEktV59zDvPu8zgGPbmtXxCjFTCZN8GhR5IEMG0LdXBQjJVcsJQsuHs9LLw6baN-q_D9dBURRk7l6psolc31J3D5s2B2_6FZEhaS2nxOqhkx6mzF7E1bdkCtRu0jkhrFlanWlbeulaU9GldAxv5i_7LUUUZBNJa72-xW3LWNwVGY7DPPCVSf92D5SUNHA~~ 
Isomorphic Labs , an A.I.-focused drug discovery start-up spun out of Google.)

The bigger issue: Google is an A.I. also-ran. Yes, it has successfully inserted its Gemini technology into its vast suite of products. It also won plaudits when its Gemini 3 model was released in November.

But its models are now considered several steps behind cutting-edge rivals from Anthropic and OpenAI. (It still hasn’t released its high-end Gemini 3.5 Pro model.)

The numbers behind Truth API
A new service selling early access to President Trump’s Truth Social posts has drawn plenty of controversy — and speculation about whether Wall Street firms will pay for it, Niko Gallogly reports.

Called Truth API, the product was created by Trump Media and Technology Group, Truth Social’s parent company.

Ten customers have signed up for Truth API so far, according to a person who is close to the company but not authorized to speak publicly about confidential information. They’re primarily trading firms whose algorithms can execute trades in fractions of a second.

For a monthly subscription fee between $60,000 and $100,000, the service alerts customers to Truth Social posts from influential accounts, including the president’s, milliseconds after the posts go up on Truth Social.

The numbers behind Truth API
A new service selling early access to President Trump’s Truth Social posts has drawn plenty of controversy — and speculation about whether Wall Street firms will pay for it, Niko Gallogly reports.

Called Truth API, the product was created by Trump Media and Technology Group, Truth Social’s parent company.

Ten customers have signed up for Truth API so far, according to a person who is close to the company but not authorized to speak publicly about confidential information. They’re primarily trading firms whose algorithms can execute trades in fractions of a second.

For a monthly subscription fee between $60,000 and $100,000, the service alerts customers to Truth Social posts from influential accounts, including the president’s, milliseconds after the posts go up on Truth Social.

The numbers behind Truth API
A new service selling early access to President Trump’s Truth Social posts has drawn plenty of controversy — and speculation about whether Wall Street firms will pay for it, Niko Gallogly reports.

Called Truth API, the product was created by Trump Media and Technology Group, Truth Social’s parent company.

Ten customers have signed up for Truth API so far, according to a person who is close to the company but not authorized to speak publicly about confidential information. They’re primarily trading firms whose algorithms can execute trades in fractions of a second.

Google’s A.I. future
Investors in Google panicked yesterday after the tech giant announced a 
https://nl.nytimes.com/f/newsletter/naGoBLpO8b4-RJ5fs07HaQ~~/AAAAARA~/w0rVAoaOrwJ19SGmeG3HlRoASTqk9tZtDzFZXRkKc5GwvYQsK0otNEpwSHEI16c8fwiIlTgXNY8TfiqO2py5pF2xks5IZnY7YSS3qP05S4wMrFwA1lzJvGfZqFDaeE8gbGcjEUP59nEOK8ucIeVnQnghHwDJOtPKWETnV4nvZ8ssAbl9hA8TELOXegm0vhNU7IruYTr-sjRvjQpG8mMMqG8YDm03hL7Kxe_tCVSmn3-ILLg_ynp3_aG4GbZTBCkW84DR6gatl70HC51FfStX9uVZEgYtM4dlaWMBuy1b8gokp9YrknmDB1NJtPXs1EPYylTKfExmR44tJdc-EHPA_mlyO7EuQRpk5DjfVGBwXKxVNYXnYdCngHdTY3e37MX2 
major shake-up  in the leadership of its artificial intelligence division, Google DeepMind, and the departure of a hugely influential scientist.

The impact of the changes may be less than it initially appeared. But Wall Street’s reaction reflects anxiety about whether Google can catch up to its A.I. rivals.

What’s happened:

	- Demis Hassabis, the C.E.O. of Google DeepMind, will become chair of the unit and chief scientist of Google’s parent company, Alphabet.
	- Koray Kavukcuoglu, a top lieutenant to Hassabis, will take over day-to-day management of Google DeepMind.
	- Jeff Dean, Google’s chief scientist, and three other colleagues are leaving to

found an A.I. start-up .

The background:

	- Hassabis had

already been delegating  day-to-day management of Google DeepMind to Kavukcuoglu, according to Semafor.
	- Dean, though revered by many Google engineers and one of the company’s earliest hires, hadn’t been at the forefront of the company’s A.I. efforts. (Sergey Brin, a Google founder, has been increasingly hands-on.) In a sign of apparent comity, Google will invest in Dean’s new start-up.

Hassabis has become one of the company’s statesmen on A.I. — he was Google’s representative at the A.I.-focused Group of 7 meeting this summer — and is increasingly focused on issues like the technology’s social impact. (He also runs

Isomorphic Labs , an A.I.-focused drug discovery start-up spun out of Google.)

The bigger issue: Google is an A.I. also-ran. Yes, it has successfully inserted its Gemini technology into its vast suite of products. It also won plaudits when its Gemini 3 model was released in November.

But its models are now considered several steps behind cutting-edge rivals from Anthropic and OpenAI. (It still hasn’t released its high-end Gemini 3.5 Pro model.)

Meanwhile, Google has continued to bleed research talent, including Noam Shazeer (to OpenAI), John Jumper (to Anthropic) and David Silver (who founded Ineffable Intelligence).

$195 billion to $205 billion  on capital expenditures (mostly A.I.-focused) this year, more than double what it did last year, and reported negative free cash flow for the first time since its I.P.O. in 2004.

The numbers behind Truth API
A new service selling early access to President Trump’s Truth Social posts has drawn plenty of controversy — and speculation about whether Wall Street firms will pay for it, Niko Gallogly reports.

Called Truth API, the product was created by Trump Media and Technology Group, Truth Social’s parent company.

Ten customers have signed up for Truth API so far, according to a person who is close to the company but not authorized to speak publicly about confidential information. They’re primarily trading firms whose algorithms can execute trades in fractions of a second.

For a monthly subscription fee between $60,000 and $100,000, the service alerts customers to Truth Social posts from influential accounts, including the president’s, milliseconds after the posts go up on Truth Social.

The numbers behind Truth API
A new service selling early access to President Trump’s Truth Social posts has drawn plenty of controversy — and speculation about whether Wall Street firms will pay for it, Niko Gallogly reports.

Called Truth API, the product was created by Trump Media and Technology Group, Truth Social’s parent company.

Ten customers have signed up for Truth API so far, according to a person who is close to the company but not authorized to speak publicly about confidential information. They’re primarily trading firms whose algorithms can execute trades in fractions of a second.

For a monthly subscription fee between $60,000 and $100,000, the service alerts customers to Truth Social posts from influential accounts, including the president’s, milliseconds after the posts go up on Truth Social.
